content.text:
You are the lead/coordinator for caliper's road to v1 alpha (Storybook integration is the product's purpose). Read first: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/memory/MEMORY.md (and the memories it links), ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md (workers' rules and the pre-push gate), AGENTS.md, and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/{REPORT,pattern-eval,pattern-eval-mui-radix,memory-split,memory-profile}.md. Date of this handoff: 2026-11-16.

## Product rule (the user's, non-negotiable)
Storybook Controls must list EVERYTHING in the component's main props even if no story uses it, plus whatever the component body itself uses directly (reads, destructures, passes explicitly; never through a DOM spread). Big generated/ambient sources (DOM/ARIA/event attributes, style-system props) stay as names in a layer. Decide by provenance and structure, never by name lists. Fix classes of problems and patterns, not one-off components ("produce the best results, not overwhelming numbers"). colorPalette staying hidden is fine. Say "the TypeScript checker (on by default)", not "add-on" (the exact wording sweep of docs/changesets is not done; confirm meaning first).
Alpha = someone installs the Storybook addon on a real design system and gets correct Controls fast on first and second start, with plain statements of what's missing; no stability/API freeze needed.

## Process rules
- Workers run in isolated worktrees; the lead pushes their branches (`git push origin <sha>:<branch>`, never force, merge main in rather than rebase), then `entire trail link 405 --branch <b> --base main --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper` (Entire opens the PR; don't `gh pr create` unless the user approves the shim/Touch ID). Publish bodies with `gh pr edit N --title ... --body-file ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/<name>.md`. Trail 404 = Chakra memory regression, 405 = relevance/collapse/Storybook usefulness.
- Pre-push gate for workers: invariants in PR body, grammar sweep with the TS checker as oracle, mutation proofs, ALLOW-list guards, `/code-review medium` awaited, `just lint doc-check machete typos`, nextest, test-checker-lane when checker code changes. Lead reruns `just lint` itself (workers' sandbox blocks pnpm).
- After a verified fix, resolve the Entire finding yourself citing commit + test: `entire trail finding list caliper/<change> --freshness=any ...`. Findings for the same class: fix the class, not the case.
- Constraints: oracle/corpus runs cost money (only when asked; `scripts/weekly.py --oracle --corpus antd --corpus shadcn` is authorized for acceptance; never --agent-eval); no files in /tmp (use ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures or $TMPDIR); no new scripts/options without CI/weekly value; workers: Sonnet for mechanical, Opus for provenance/design, caps on tool calls, no polling CI, max 3 parallel workers; release actions (rerun, delete assets, re-dispatch, RELEASE_PENDING_FROM) need the user's say-so; measure peak RSS and time for resolver/checker changes; git inside worktree sessions: plain single commands, no `cd` to other worktrees, no compound `$(...)`.
- Never merge or release anything without the user's approval; the user approves/merges PRs.

## State
Merged on main: Chakra 42 GB fix, collapse default 'dependencies', scheduler S1/S2, factory own props, relevance output, #491 (instantiation memory), #489 (alpha limits docs), #487 (Wisp v5).
Open PRs (all BLOCKED on CI/approval at last look):
- #490 `feat/list-props-by-usage` (change 288, trail 405): T4 listing rule (main props + body use). Remote head cf51133b. Acceptance (oracle-run/accept/accept.sh) passed 5/5 on it: Storybook Button 21 rows (20 + children), Badge children/asChild/variant, shadcn 98.7%/0 wrong, antd 93.0%/1 wrong; differential 0 violations on 7 corpora; peak RSS shadcn 879 / Chakra 1,627 MiB. TWO OPEN ENTIRE FINDINGS (one class: explicit selection not seen by both owners): chain.rs:597-599 (checker keep-and-merge must include body-promoted notable props; types/semantic.rs LayerFacts::of / layer_notable) and relevance/props_type.rs:164-165 (substitute generic-alias args when collecting picked keys). A worker (agent ace6850035594237c, worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-ace6850035594237c, branch fix/list-rule-patterns) was mid-fix when the session ended; check its worktree (`git status`, `git log`), finish or restart: class fix with grammar sweep + model test that every visible structural row survives the checker merge + mutation proofs, then push to feat/list-props-by-usage and resolve both findings. Afterwards, separate commits: change 8 (no analysable body = unknown, keep what main listed: MUI .d.ts components lose className/style/ref), change 7 (hook hand-off useX(props) as forwarding), D (Chakra fixture still ~865 rows: the `declined` guard blocks the generated rule; decide if the guard is right). Evidence: pattern-eval.md lists 7 rule-level changes (1-6 done in #490: ambient by declaring interface, member ambient only if all declarations ambient, generated rule for project sources, reads promote from large layers, mapped-copy by key interface nature, one-hop aliases).
- #492 `fix/weekly-oracle-measurement` (change 290): Node heap 16 GB for Chakra oracle, "not judged" as its own column, headline over judged props, coverage floor 50% (new gate: ask the user whether it stays), recall counts layer names.
- Change 291 `perf/converter-memo-interning` (HEAD 1335c3d2 pushed, linked to trail 405): converter memo interning, Chakra peak 1,690 -> 1,366 MiB, output identical. NO PR was opened by Entire yet; check `gh pr list --head perf/converter-memo-interning --state all`; if still none ask the user (shim needs Touch ID). Publish body from ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/perf-converter-memo-interning.md.
- #497 callisto/version-packages (release PR, not reviewed), #493-#496 dependabot.

## Next
1. Land #490's findings fix (above), push, check CI/Entire, resolve findings, rerun accept.sh on the new head: `zsh ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/accept/accept.sh <bin> <packages/storybook dir with napi build> <label>`; MUI/Radix: `oracle-run/pattern-eval/run-extra.sh <main-bin> <490-bin>`.
2. Chakra memory: ~1.1-1.2 GiB expected after #491 + memo interning; under 1 GiB needs more converter work (memory-split.md parts), not required for alpha.
3. Weekly: merge #492 then run the oracle once on merged main (idle machine), refresh docs/STATUS.md speed numbers; weekly "not judged" cause (Chakra 75.5%, Mantine 62.9%) undiagnosed.
4. Unmeasured: Storybook prefetch, antd in Storybook (Vite `./version` import fails), head-to-head vs react-docgen-typescript.
5. MUI `Button`/`Select` (OverridableComponent/ExtendButtonBase declare const) aren't extracted by either binary: separate extraction gap, ask the user if it should be a slice.

## Needs the user's decision (ask early)
- 0.11.0 release recovery (E167 ArtifactAssetDiffers): delete mismatched asset + `gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha=<sha>`, or skip via RELEASE_PENDING_FROM; is #497 the vehicle? (corpora budget gate never ran on a real release PR.)
- Should the addon default flip (collapseInheritedProps 'dependencies') ship in the first alpha? Alpha audience? Coverage floor on the weekly (#492)? Worktree cleanup: ~60 stale worktrees under .claude/worktrees (peer session cleanup-merged-branches-worktrees did a sweep; don't remove live ones).

Start by checking `gh pr list`, `gh pr checks 490`, Entire findings for caliper/288, 290, 291, and the worker worktree state, then continue with step 1 and report.
Starting with the memory index, worker contract, and current PR/worktree state.

content.text:
Both #288 findings are fixed, pushed to #490 and resolved. #288 now has no open findings, and CI is running on the new head.

**Where the fix lives:**
- Branch `feat/list-props-by-usage` is at `453f2aea` (three commits on top of `cf51133b`, a fast-forward push).
- The fix is the class, not the two cases: every owner now reads the same answer for "which props are visible rows".
- Chain.rs:597-599: the checker merges take exactly the members the structural answer keeps typed. Body-promoted members count as visible rows.
- props_type.rs:164-165: generic aliases over a key set are instantiated with their arguments. An `Omit` alias is read like an inline `Omit`. A `Pick` with unproven keys narrows nothing.

**Checks run:**
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`, workspace nextest (1690 passed) and `just test-checker-lane` all exited 0 on the final tree.
- Five mutation proofs each fail a named test. Two of them survived at first, so I added tests that pin them.
- The first review round came from the worker. My `/code-review medium` found six issues: I fixed two (dead helpers deleted, duplicated default policy removed) and dismissed three as intended behaviour or already covered. The sixth, a possible performance cost, I measured. Release builds of `cf51133b` and the new head on `gate-large` and `chakra-only`, three runs each, gave the same output, peak memory within 15 MiB and times within noise (load average was around 29). That was the structural-only extract with no checker, so Chakra's 1.6 GiB checker-lane peak was not re-measured.

**Why I set rustup and mise variables:** I copied them from the worker contract, which says the mise shim forces Rust 1.98.1. Plain `rustc` already gives 1.99.1 here, so they were unnecessary, and I'll stop using them. The checks themselves went through `just`. The repo has a `justfile` and an empty `.moon` directory, but no `moon.yml`, so I don't see any moon tasks to use.

**Still to do:**
- Read the CI result when the background wait finishes. Entire Gates may raise new findings.
- Rerun `accept.sh` on `453f2aea` (the authorized antd and shadcn oracle) and the MUI/Radix `run-extra.sh`. I held both until CI settles.
- Then the separate commits: change 8, change 7, and D (whether the Chakra `declined` guard is right).

**One deviation:** the worker's fix-round edits were uncommitted in that worktree, so I verified them against the diff and committed them.

## What

Without the TypeScript checker, an enum member whose value the extractor could not evaluate was typed as its own name: `enum Level { Low = 1 << 2 }` made `Level.Low` the string `"Low"`, and the `enums` output listed `"value": "Low"`.

- An unevaluable member is now `EnumValue::Unknown` (serialized `null`), never a literal, so `Level.Low` stays unresolved.
- The extractor folds the initializers TypeScript folds (parentheses, unary `+ - ~`, arithmetic, shifts, bitwise operators, string concatenation, substitution-free templates, reads of earlier members of the same enum), so `1 << 2` is now `4`.
- Cache schema 45 -> 46.

Breaking for `caliper-docgen-core`: `EnumValue` has a new `Unknown` variant and `EnumValue::to_display_string` returns `Option<String>`. The changeset says so.

The bug is on main since b19f8e1e. It was found by an Entire finding on change 291 (#499), which does not touch this code.

## Evidence

Run by the lead on 22baa273, detached, in its own worktree:
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 1696 passed, 3 skipped, exit 0.
- `just test-checker-lane`: exit 0.
- Repro on the `cf51133b` release build with `--no-checker`: `Level.Low` was `stringLiteral "Low"`.

## Not verified

- Mutation proofs, `just semver`, `/code-review medium` and a grammar sweep of the new constant folder (`extractor/enum_fold.rs`) were not run on this commit.
- No Chakra or Mantine output comparison.
- Output change: unknown members print `value: null` in `enums`. Consumers of that field were not audited beyond `packages/napi/index.d.ts`.

Both findings are fixed and resolved, and the failing check on #502 has a fix pushed. CI is still running on #502 and #504, and I'm waiting on it once in the background.

**Change 302, the surrogate finding (#504):**
- `f20629e7` is pushed as a fast-forward.
- A string with a lone surrogate is now unresolved in the enum folder, whether it is a literal, a template or a computed-member key. `"\uD83D" + "\uDE00"` stays unresolved instead of publishing two replacement characters. A surrogate pair inside one literal still folds to the emoji.
- Putting back either the lossy text conversion or the lossy key lookup fails a test (`an_enum_member_the_structural_lane_cannot_fold_is_not_its_own_name`, `a_member_read_by_a_key_with_a_lone_surrogate_is_unresolved`).
- Lint, doc-check, machete, typos (after `cargo fmt`) and the workspace nextest (1698 passed) exit 0.
- I resolved the Entire finding.

**Change 300 (#502, dependabot):**
- The failing job was "Test / Vite plugin on the native binding". Its `tsc` step in `packages/storybook` couldn't find Node types.
- TypeScript 7 includes no `@types` package unless `tsconfig` lists it. On main, Node types only reached `tsc` through something inside storybook beta.0, and beta.1 dropped it. I reproduced the failure locally.
- The fix is `"types": ["node"]` in `packages/storybook/tsconfig.json`; `tsc` then exits 0 and `just lint` exits 0.
- I pushed `3faaf5e1` straight onto the dependabot branch as a fast-forward, which may stop dependabot from auto-rebasing that PR.
- I did not run the storybook integration test locally, only `tsc`, so CI is the check for the rest.

Restored from my reading of `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md` (deleted by the user 2026-11-17; see [[fixtures-is-not-scratch]]). Changes made while restoring: no build output or scratch in `caliper-fixtures`; PR bodies go in `$TMPDIR` or the worktree, not there.

**Scope**: edit only the files the brief names; if another must change, stop and say which and why. Never ask the user questions; if blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work.

**Branch and push**: branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Build in the worktree's own `target/` (the `just test-checker-lane` recipe hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`). Plain `rustc` is 1.99.1 here; the old note about the mise shim forcing 1.98.1 did not reproduce on 2026-11-17. Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: <session url>`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, fully qualified when pushing a bare SHA), never `--no-verify`, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Workers do not open or edit the PR and do not poll CI.

**Checks, targeted (CI runs the rest)**: always before push `just lint doc-check machete typos`. Then only what the change touches: Rust -> nextest of touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once (run it without a CARGO_TARGET_DIR override); checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against a build of origin/main on a large fixture and a Chakra-only fixture. Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless that area changed. Tests must fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one. No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, prefer allocation or instruction counts.

**Cap**: stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what is verified; "not done, because X" beats burning calls.

**Artifacts**: PR body with `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line the session url; the lead publishes it unedited. Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers.

**Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new)**:
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms; everything else is Unknown/Declined (never "complete", "none", "exact"). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried (cargo mutants --in-diff works).
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types, lone surrogates).

content.text:
The history is large because of Entire's session recording, not the code. Of the 266 MiB of blob data on disk, 256 MiB is session logs and only 10 MiB is source, snapshots and metadata.

- **Session logs:** Entire stores every checkpoint's transcript (`full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl`) and every subagent's task log in git, under `refs/entire/checkpoints`. That namespace has 2,585 refs (checkpoint snapshots in the local clone). The largest single transcript is 29 MB, and every blob in the top 15 is one. import os, subprocess, collections

root = os.path.expanduser("~/Projects")
names = {"target": "target", "dist": "dist", "node_modules": "node_modules", ".next": ".next", "coverage": "coverage"}
found = []
for dirpath, dirnames, _ in os.walk(root):
    depth = dirpath[len(root):].count(os.sep)
    keep = []
    for d in dirnames:
        if d in names:
            found.append((os.path.join(dirpath, d), names[d]))
        elif d != ".git" and depth < 6:
            keep.append(d)
    dirnames[:] = keep


def kb(path):
    out = subprocess.run(["du", "-sk", path], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
    return int(out[0]) if out else 0


by_kind = collections.Counter()
by_repo = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.Counter())
rows = []
for path, kind in found:
    size = kb(path)
    by_kind[kind] += size
    repo = path[len(root) + 1:].split(os.sep)[0]
    by_repo[repo][kind] += size
    rows.append((size, path))
print("BY KIND (GB):", {k: round(v / 1048576, 1) for k, v in by_kind.most_common()})

rows.sort(reverse=True)
print("TOP 12:")
for size, path in rows[:12]:

caliper = [r for r in rows if "/caliper/" in r[1] or r[1].startswith(root + "/caliper")]
print("caliper dirs:", len(caliper), "total GB", round(sum(s for s, _ in caliper) / 1048576, 1))

You're right: nothing cleans up `target` after a worktree goes dormant. `target` is 175.6 GB across your projects; `dist` is only 0.5 GB and `node_modules` 14.8 GB (mostly `pages`, 8.2 GB), so `dist` isn't the problem.

**Where it sits:**
- **callisto:** 80 GB, mostly one `target` per agent worktree (11–14 GB each).
- **monokl:** 50 GB.
- **gix:** 13 GB in one worktree.
- **panda and michi:** about 10–12 GB each.
- **caliper:** 7.3 GB, which I just trimmed.

**What I cleaned in caliper:** I deleted `target` in four dormant worktrees (`abdd35c`, `ae96c08`, `a518d0c8`, `dep-502`), about 2.7 GB. `.claude/worktrees` is now 8.6 GB, 4.7 GB of which is the live build in `memo-interning`. I left `node_modules` alone (pnpm shares files with its store, so `du` overstates what it costs on disk). I did not touch the other repos' targets, because callisto has an active session working in it.

**Why it keeps happening:**
- Every worktree builds its own `target`.
- Caliper's dev profile uses full debug info, so each `target` is 4–5 GB, and a release and test build adds more.
- Nothing removes `target` when a worktree stops being used. It only goes when the worktree is removed.

**What I'd change, in order of payoff (none made yet):**
1. **Smaller builds:** set `[profile.dev]` and `[profile.test]` to `debug = "line-tables-only"` in caliper's `Cargo.toml`. It would roughly halve each `target`, but I haven't measured it, so I'd measure first. This is a small PR, and the same change works in callisto, monokl and the others.
2. **One shared target directory for workers:** point agents at one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per repo. Dependencies are the bulk and get reused, and the cost is lock waits when two builds overlap. This needs a one-line fix to the `test-checker-lane` recipe, which hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`.
3. **A cleanup rule:** remove a worktree, and its `target`, as soon as its PR merges. I now do this at merge time and will keep doing it.

- From the props type: explicit own members always; the keys of Pick<X, 'a' | 'b'> (named on purpose; Omit says nothing about the rest); members that override or narrow a base member; JSDoc, @default and literal-union members; required members.
- Spreads: {...rest} on a DOM tag means the ambient DOM attributes (ignore, the layer covers it). A spread onto a component (<Primitive {...rest} />) means that component's own, non-ambient props may be this component's props: resolve the JSX tag to its component, one hop, own props only; the collapse threshold still applies. Unresolvable targets and useX(props) stay unknown.
- Minus what the component passes directly: attributes set after the spread are fixed (a later attribute wins), so subtract them; attributes set before the spread are overridable defaults, keep them; an attribute whose value comes from the component's own props (size={props.size}) is the component's own declared prop, already shown.

Mostly yes, and it's more than the oracle. The real sample libraries are fetched by a script, not kept in `caliper-fixtures`.

**What was in `caliper-fixtures`:** it was a mix of four things, built up over the project by me and the workers.
- **Reference corpora:** real design-system repos (antd, shadcn, chakra, mantine, mui, radix, panda). The weekly oracle run and the acceptance runs read these.
- **Test inputs for the gate tools:** `gate-large/src` and `checker-default/chakra-only/src`, used for the output-identity diffs and the memory and time measurements.
- **Per-task scratch:** worker outputs, perf comparisons, red-team inputs, and the build output I put there.
- **Process notes:** the worker contract, the oracle-run reports, and the PR bodies.

Only the first group is what you mean by sample libraries, and the repo already handles it without that directory.
- **In-repo fixtures:** `fixtures/` in the repo holds 23 small sample libraries (antd, ariakit, chakra, radix, shadcn and others) at 404 KB total. The construct suite (254 fixtures) and CI use these.
- **Real corpora:** `scripts/corpora.py setup` clones the pinned real repos. By default it puts them in `.corpora/repos` inside the repo, and `weekly.py --corpora DIR` can point elsewhere. It does not need `caliper-fixtures`.

So the oracle, corpora and tests don't depend on that directory. The weekly run can re-clone the corpora with `scripts/corpora.py setup`. `.corpora` should be gitignored. I haven't checked that, or its size.

**What is lost for good:**
- The worker contract, now saved to memory.
- The oracle-run reports and `pattern-eval.md`, which hold the evidence for changes 8, 7 and D.
- `accept.sh`, which was a one-off harness. Its checks (CLI rows, Storybook Controls rows, oracle headline) are what I'd rebuild from `REPORT.md`, if that is recovered.
- The gate inputs (`gate-large` and the Chakra-only fixture), which I'd rebuild from `.corpora`, not restore.

**Recommendation:**
- Don't restore the whole directory.
- If you restore anything from the snapshot, take only the `oracle-run/*.md` reports and `worker-contract.md`, a few MB in total. That would keep the evidence for changes 8, 7 and D.
- Use `.corpora` as the re-clonable cache for the real libraries.
- Put anything that should last in the repo, such as the contract in `docs/` and the acceptance checks in `apps/oracle` or CI.
- Keep temporary output in `$TMPDIR`.

I haven't confirmed that CI or `weekly.py` uses the real corpora from `.corpora` rather than anything from the old directory. I saw only that `--corpora` defaults to `.corpora/repos`.
Why were these things outside of the repo? Were we over-engineering and it's fine or should they have been part of the repo? Should we have a separate repo to support the oracle?

They were outside the repo for a reason, but only part of it holds up. I'm inferring the history from the files and my memory notes, not from a record of the decision.

**Why they were outside:** one of your earlier rules, saved in my memory, says not to add scripts, options or recipes to the repo unless CI or the weekly run uses them. Per-task work, harnesses and logs therefore had nowhere to go but outside. The worker contract then told every worker to put its build directory and scratch in `caliper-fixtures/<task>/`. I followed it, which led to roughly 90 per-task directories and several GB of build output.

**What holds up and what doesn't:**
- Throwaway output was right to keep out of the repo: logs, A/B binaries, red-team inputs, per-task diffs.
- Process knowledge was wrong to leave there, and the deletion shows it. That means the worker contract, the oracle reports and the evidence behind changes 8, 7 and D. Decisions belong in an ADR or `docs/`, and PR bodies are already on GitHub.
- `accept.sh` is a harness we re-ran for every acceptance and will need again. Under your own rule it belongs in `apps/oracle`, because we use it repeatedly. A one-off doesn't need to be in the repo, but this one wasn't one-off.
- Real corpora being outside the repo is correct, since they are cloned and pinned by `scripts/corpora.py`.

**A separate repo for the oracle: no.**
- The oracle already lives in the repo: `apps/oracle` (the construct suite, checker lane and parity checks), `scripts/weekly.py`, and `scripts/corpora.py`.
- A second repo would add cross-repo version pinning and a second CI for no gain.
- The one case that might justify it is a large history of recorded benchmark results. I haven't seen how big that is, and `weekly.json` and `weekly.md` are in the oracle-run directory that is gone. I'd keep it in the repo until the data actually gets large.

**Proposed split:**
- **Repo:** harnesses we re-run, decisions and the worker contract (in `docs/`), and pinned corpus definitions.
- **`.corpora`:** a re-clonable cache, gitignored.
- **`$TMPDIR`:** throwaway scratch, nothing in it needed later.
- **Per-task directories:** none.

The plan below rests on what I measured today. I changed nothing.

**Where things stand**
- **Worktrees:** down from 68 to 7, and `.claude` is 1.8 GB. I didn't prune them; you or a peer session did.
- **Largest local disk users:** `~/Projects/callisto` is 74 GB. It is a different repo, but it is the biggest thing on your disk. `~/.rustup` is 10 GB, the pnpm store 7.3 GB, `~/.cargo` 2 GB and `~/.cache` 3.1 GB.
- **Already in place:** `.corpora/` is gitignored. Moon is configured (`.moon/tasks.yml`) alongside the justfile.
- **Per-worktree corpora:** `scripts/corpora.py` defaults to `.corpora/repos` under the repo root (`ROOT`). If `ROOT` is the checkout, every worktree re-clones the corpora. I haven't verified that `ROOT` is the checkout.

**What goes where: by lifetime**
1. **In the repo:**
   - Code we re-run: the acceptance harness in `apps/oracle`, and `scripts/`.
   - Decisions and process: ADRs, the worker contract, and the acceptance checks in `docs/`.
   - Small real test inputs: `fixtures/`, 404 KB today.
   - The pinned corpus definitions.
2. **Re-creatable cache:** safe to delete at any time. That means `target/`, `node_modules`, and the cloned corpora. The corpora should be one shared copy outside any worktree, such as `~/.cache/caliper/corpora`.
3. **Run outputs worth keeping:** the weekly record goes to `docs/STATUS.md`, as the handoff already says. Acceptance results go in the PR body. Raw JSON is dropped.
4. **Throwaway:** logs, A/B binaries, diffs. These go in the job's `$TMPDIR` and are gone when the job ends.
5. **Never recorded:** personal files or secrets.

**Naming:** a location holds what its name says. Anything outside the repo is named for its purpose and documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Nothing lives under `Projects/` except checkouts.

**Disk and caching:**
- **Fewer worktrees:** keep at most four live ones. At about 5 GB each (the 4.7 GB `target` plus about 400 MB `node_modules`), that is about 20 GB.
- **Shared corpora:** the one cache directory above.
- **Cargo:** sharing a target directory serializes builds on cargo's lock and causes rebuilds across different checkouts. I'd try `sccache` for compiled dependencies and keep a separate `target/` per worktree.
- **Debug info:** setting it to `line-tables-only` would shrink `target/`, but I haven't measured by how much. I'd measure first.

**Cleanup, as a documented routine and not a script,** because of your no-new-scripts rule. After each merged batch:
1. Remove worktrees that are merged, pushed and clean.
2. Delete `target/` in worktrees idle for a few days.
3. Run `git worktree prune`.
4. Delete the merged local branches (76 today).
5. Run `entire clean`.

**Separate from this:** moon and just both define fmt, lint and typos, and I haven't compared the two. The Entire logs in `.git` are a different problem.

28	OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
29	```
30	
31	No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).
32	
33	See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.
34	
35	## Decisions
36	
37	Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.
38	
39	## Testing discipline
40	
41	Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):
42	
43	1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
44	2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.
45	
46	## Crate guide
47	
48	- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
49	- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
50	- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core
51	- `crates/semantic` — TypeScript 7.1 checker backend, on by default (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`)
52	
53	## Scripts
54	
55	No new sh, py or mjs script unless a CI job, the weekly or a documented recipe calls it; prefer a Rust test or the existing oracle TypeScript. A measurement run once is recorded in docs (`docs/measurement.md`, `docs/gate-measurements.md`), not committed as a script. Each script's caller is listed in `docs/measurement.md`.
56	
57	## Plugins
58	
59	Start work with `/wisp:work`, or the mode directly so its checks run:
60	
61	- Options before deciding: `/wisp:explore`. Does it work: `/wisp:spike`.
62	- Bug or review findings: `/wisp:fix`. Real feature or shared change: `/wisp:build`.
63	- Verify or find bugs: `/wisp:check`. Commit, changeset or release: `/wisp:ship`.
64	
65	State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list.
66	
67	Packs: rust-house, ts-house
68	
69	Pull requests are opened by Entire from the branch's trail, so `/wisp:ship` stops at the commit: push the branch and create or link its trail (`entire trail create`). Do not open the PR with `gh`.
70	
71	## Writing and commits
72	
73	- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
74	- Changesets live in `.changeset/` as one file per consumer-visible topic, with a front matter line per affected package (`cargo/caliper-docgen: patch`, `npm/caliper-docgen: minor`). Changesets become the project's changelog, so write them for the people who use it, not for the implementer.
75	  - Open with a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, then one line on its value: what they can now do or what changed for them.
76	  - When there is more to say, add short bullets in this order: why it matters, how to adopt it (commands, configuration, migration), and limits they will hit. Use sub-bullets for detail.
77	  - Group a longer entry under bold labels such as **Upgrading** or **Scripting**. Do not use `#` headings; the changelog supplies those.
78	  - Put a breaking change in its own paragraph starting `**Breaking:**` (old behavior, new behavior, what to do), and a step users must take in one starting `**Action:**`. Never inside a bullet: the release PR lists them under "Read before merging" only as paragraphs.
79	  - One idea per bullet. Leave out internals unless the user must know them.
80	- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
81	- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
82	- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.
83

# Measurement

Two things, both small: a weekly record of how Caliper compares with react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on five public repos, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. Nothing here blocks a pull request.

## Weekly record

`.github/workflows/weekly.yml` runs on Mondays and by hand. `scripts/corpora.py` fetches each repo at a pinned commit and installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile (lifecycle scripts off, caches under `.corpora/`, gitignored), then removes tests, stories, demos and the `dist/` and `build/` directories from the source directory so every tool reads the same files. `scripts/weekly.py` runs the tools.

Declaration files are kept. Until 2026-11 the fetch also deleted every `.d.ts`, which removed a corpus's own type packages: React Spectrum declares `@react-types/shared` in `packages/@react-types/shared/src/*.d.ts` and its components import from it. With those files gone, 20 props that reach a component through `Pick` of a name declared there were lost; on unmodified main with the files restored, Caliper reports 20 of 20. Generated declarations sit in `dist/` and `build/`, which are still removed. A fetched corpus records a prune version in its marker (`PRUNE_VERSION` in `scripts/corpora.py`), so one pruned under the older rule is fetched again on the next `setup`; `--sparse` never pruned and already kept declaration files. The first weekly run after this change moves Caliper's and RDT's numbers on every corpus whose source tree holds `.d.ts` files (React Spectrum has 67 under `packages/`).

| Corpus | Repository | Commit | Source directory | Install |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mantine | `mantinedev/mantine` | `e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d` | `packages/@mantine/core/src` | yarn, immutable |
| chakra | `chakra-ui/chakra-ui` | `fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9` | `packages/react/src` | pnpm, frozen |
| shadcn | `shadcn-ui/ui` | `ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b` | `apps/v4` | pnpm, frozen |
| antd | `ant-design/ant-design` | `ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538` | `components` | npm, no lockfile (the repo commits none) |
| spectrum | `adobe/react-spectrum` | `797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70` | `packages` | yarn, immutable |

It records, per corpus and tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start and Node start included), and the size of Caliper's canonical JSON. Caliper runs with `--load-dependencies` and the default, the checker (ADR 0026's S8); its time is the median of five runs. The record (time, memory, recall and the oracle's verdicts) is the checker's, and `oracle.universe_version` 5 marks the change: a record of version 4 or earlier is the structural resolver's (`--no-checker`), its wrong types and agreement are not compared with the checker's, and its time and memory are not budgets for it. The structural resolver is not run weekly; its speed (34 to 81 ms on a whole library, `docs/performance.md`) was measured by hand. RDT and react-docgen run once each.

### The budgets

The checker's whole-project run takes seconds and several hundred MiB to a GiB, so the 2 s and 600 MiB of the structural record no longer apply. `BUDGETS` in `scripts/headline.py` holds a time and a peak-memory limit for each corpus, set after 0.11.0 shipped the checker as the default and needed 42 GB on the real Chakra corpus (`chakra-ui/packages/react/src`): nothing ran the corpora before that release, and the first weekly died on it (exit 143) and left no record. They are "something is badly wrong" limits, not tuning. Each is 4 times the time and 2 times the peak memory measured on the fixed build (release binary, checker on, cold cache, one run at load 7 to 20 on an Apple M5 Max), because a GitHub runner is slower and smaller than that Mac:

| Corpus                        | Measured | Time budget | Measured RSS | RSS budget |

1	# Contributing
2	
3	By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.
4	
5	## Prerequisites
6	
7	| Tool  | Min version   | Notes                                         |
8	| ----- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
9	| Rust  | 1.99          | `rustup update stable`                        |
10	| proto | latest        | manages Node/pnpm versions from `.prototools` |
11	| pnpm  | `.prototools` | via proto, or `npm i -g pnpm`                 |
12	
13	After installing proto, run `moon setup` once to pull the pinned Node version and any other tool versions declared in `.prototools`.
14	
15	## Build & test
16	
17	```bash
18	# Rust
19	cargo build                                            # dev build
20	cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core                   # unit + snapshot tests
21	cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
22	cargo fmt --all
23	
24	# TypeScript
25	pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test      # unit tests (mocked NAPI)
26	pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration  # integration tests (real native binding)
27	
28	# Speed and memory of your branch against origin/main (Mantine and Chakra)
29	just bench
30	```
31	
32	The pre-commit hook runs `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `typos`, and `cargo deny` on every commit. It's fast enough that skipping it isn't worth the trouble.
33	
34	## Snapshot tests
35	
36	Snapshot tests use [insta](https://insta.rs). Each fixture (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, etc.) has a snapshot of the full extraction output. If your change touches extraction output, insta will flag it:
37	
38	```bash
39	cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core    # fails with "snapshot mismatch"
40	cargo insta review                     # review diffs, accept or reject
41	```
42	
43	Accept any snapshot change that is intentional (i.e., the output got more accurate). Reject regressions.
44	
45	## Where code goes
46	
47	**`crates/core`** — everything that understands TypeScript ASTs and React component patterns. No I/O, no async, no terminal output. Every function here must be `Send + Sync` so rayon can parallelize it.
48	
49	**`crates/cli`** — user-facing output only. No extraction logic. Commands parse args and delegate to `core::pipeline`. Error formatting uses `miette`; progress uses `indicatif`; table output uses `comfy-table`.
50	
51	**`crates/binding`** — thin NAPI wrapper. Owns the async runtime (tokio) and exposes the NAPI functions listed in `packages/napi/binding.d.ts` (batch extraction, sessions, and the lazy session's index, answers and warm-up). No business logic.
52	
53	**`packages/napi`** — `caliper-docgen-napi`. TypeScript types (`index.d.ts`) and the dev binary loader (`index.js`) that finds the `.node` file from `target/` or `NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH`. No logic.
54	
55	**`packages/vite-plugin`** — `caliper-docgen-vite-plugin`. Single Vite `Plugin` object. No extraction logic — calls NAPI and manages HMR.
56	
57	## Code style
58	
59	The authoritative reference is `.claude/skills/rust-style/SKILL.md`. Highlights:
60	
61	**Maps:** `FxHashMap` for internal maps (hot path, no DoS surface). `BTreeMap` for anything that ends up in JSON output (key ordering must be deterministic and stable across runs).
62	
63	**Strings:** `CompactString` for type names and prop names. Most are ≤24 bytes (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`) and fit inline without heap allocation.
64	
65	**Control flow:** `let...else` keeps the happy path flat:
66	
67	```rust
68	let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
69	```
70	
71	**Matching on project-local enums:** no wildcards. `match status { Ok => .., Err => .. }` gives a compile error when new variants are added. `match status { Ok => .., _ => .. }` silently ignores them.
72	
73	**No `unwrap()` outside tests.** Use `?` or emit a `Diagnostic` and return a safe default. The `Diagnostic` type has constructors for common error shapes.
74	
75	**Comments:** only when the WHY is non-obvious. Not what the code does.
76	
77	## Commits
78	
79	- GPG-signed, `Signed-off-by` trailer (both configured in `.git/config`). `main` requires signed commits, so an unsigned commit in a pull request blocks the merge.
80	- `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` prefix
81	- No line wrapping at any column
82	- Subject line says it all — skip the body if it adds nothing
83	
84	```
85	# good
86	feat: resolve ComponentPropsWithoutRef in intersection type aliases
87	
88	# bad
89	Updated the resolver to also handle the case where ComponentPropsWithoutRef
90	appears inside an intersection type alias, which was causing it to be
91	treated as opaque when it should expand the HTML attributes.
92	```
93	
94	## Releases
95	
96	Add a changeset for a consumer-visible change (`.changeset/`; see `AGENTS.md` for how to write one). Callisto (version pinned in `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`) plans the versions from the changesets and opens a release pull request (`callisto/version-packages`); merging it runs `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, which publishes the crates and npm packages, tags each package, and publishes one GitHub Release for the CLI (`cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z`) with its changelog section as the notes and the five CLI binaries attached, each with a build attestation. The npm wrapper's tag `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` is what the tap reads. `docs/releasing.md` has the release flow and how to recover a failed run.
97	
98	Homebrew pulls from us: the tap's daily `brew bump` finds that tag with `livecheck`, builds `crates/cli` from source and bottles it, and a maintainer merges the formula pull request. Nothing in this repository notifies the tap.
99	
100	Speed, memory and accuracy are recorded weekly and compared with the previous run (`docs/measurement.md`); there is no pull-request gate. Run `just bench` when a change touches the resolver.
101	
102	## Pull requests
103	
104	1. Branch from `main`
105	2. Keep the pre-commit hook passing
106	3. Update snapshots if extraction output changes (`cargo insta review`)
107	4. One logical change per PR — squash fixup commits before merging
108	
109	> `just bench` is a local check of speed and memory against `main`; it prints a table and fails nothing. Accuracy against RDT and react-docgen is tracked by the weekly record (`docs/measurement.md`), not by a pull-request gate.

## Local disk, caches and worktrees

Each place holds one kind of thing, and its name says which.

- **The repository:** code we re-run (`scripts/`, `apps/oracle`), decisions (`docs/adr/`), process (this file, `AGENTS.md`), and small test inputs (`fixtures/`). Anything a later change or a reviewer needs goes here, or in the pull request description.
- **Caches you can delete at any time:** `target/`, `node_modules/`, and `.corpora/` (the weekly's pinned repos, gitignored; `docs/measurement.md`). Deleting one costs rebuild or download time and nothing else. A worktree's `target/` was about 5 GB and its `node_modules/` about 400 MB when this was written.
- **Throwaway output:** logs, A/B binaries, diffs. Write them under `$TMPDIR`, which is not kept. If you need a result later, record it in the pull request or in `docs/`.
- **Nothing outside the repository is kept for the project.** Do not create a directory under `~/Projects` for output, and do not store build output in a directory named for something else (a `fixtures` directory holds test inputs only).

`just test-checker-lane` builds into `target/release` of the current checkout and reads the binary from there, so run it without `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set.

Each worktree has its own `target/`, `node_modules/` and `.corpora/`. To share one copy of the corpora between worktrees, pass `--corpora DIR` to `scripts/corpora.py` and `scripts/weekly.py`. Keep few worktrees: after a branch is merged and pushed, remove its worktree (`git worktree remove`), delete the local branch, and run `git worktree prune`.

## Before you push a behavior change

`just lint doc-check machete typos` must pass, plus the tests of the crates you touched. CI runs the rest. A change that decides something about types or props (relevance, resolution, merging) also needs:

- **Invariants:** state them in the pull request description: unknown unless proven, by binding and not by spelling, every read recorded, one owner for each decision, wired or not defined.
- **Allow-lists:** a guard handles a closed set of proven forms, and everything else is unknown or declined, never "complete", "none" or "exact". No `_ =>` arm in a decision over node or type kinds.
- **Grammar sweep:** list every syntax or type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined. Prefer a generated test over the grammar with the TypeScript checker as the oracle (`crates/semantic/tests/`) to a hand-picked list. Cover lone surrogates, computed keys, shadowing, `declare`, overloads and re-exports.
- **Mutation proof:** remove each guard in turn; a test must fail. `cargo mutants --in-diff <diff>` finds the ones no test notices.
- **A test that fails on `main`** for every behavior change.
- **Output-preserving change:** diff `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against a build of `main` on a large project and on Chakra, with `stats` removed. For resolver or checker changes, also compare peak memory and time with `just bench`, because a size regression can pass every test.
- **Findings:** when an automated or human review finds a defect, fix the class it belongs to, not only the case, and resolve the finding with the commit and test that fix it.

## Snapshot tests

## What

Two sections in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, from the worker rules that lived only outside the repository.

- **Local disk, caches and worktrees:** what the repository holds, what is a cache you can delete (`target/`, `node_modules/`, `.corpora/`), where throwaway output goes (`$TMPDIR`), that nothing outside the repository is kept for the project, how to share one corpora copy between worktrees (`--corpora DIR`), and when to remove a worktree. It also says to run `just test-checker-lane` without `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, because the recipe reads `target/release` of the checkout.
- **Before you push a behavior change:** the bar for changes that decide something about types or props. Invariants in the description, allow-list guards, a grammar sweep with the TypeScript checker as oracle, a mutation proof (`cargo mutants --in-diff`), a test that fails on `main`, an output diff and a memory and time check for resolver changes, and fixing the class of a finding, not the case.

## Evidence

- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- Checked against the repository: `scripts/corpora.py` and `scripts/weekly.py` both take `--corpora` and default to `.corpora/repos` under the checkout (`ROOT` is the directory above `scripts/`); `.corpora/`, `target/` and `node_modules/` are gitignored; `just bench` exists.
- The 5 GB and 400 MB figures are from one worktree measured on 2026-11-17 (4.7 GB `target/`, about 400 MB `node_modules/`).

## Not verified

- No code changes, so no behavior to test.
- I did not check that every sentence of the bar matches what CI enforces; it is the standard reviewers apply, not a gate.
- The acceptance harness used to compare Controls rows and the oracle headline is not in the repository and is not described here. It was in a directory that has been deleted.

- This is the "unknown unless proven" rule for a missing body, and it needs no name lists.
- It covers MUI's `.d.ts` components, though `Button` and `Select` also have a separate extraction gap I'll report on afterwards.

**One check before I write code:** whether the pre-#490 baseline really listed `className` and `style` for these components. If it didn't, then change 8 is only about `ref`, or isn't needed. I'll compare the two builds when the baseline finishes and tell you which it is before I change anything.

content.text:
Change D has a diagnosed root cause and a tested fix, still uncommitted. The main build for comparison is running in the background.

**Root cause (Chakra fixture, 878 rows per `Button`):** about 850 of those rows were csstype style interfaces, reached through `React.CSSProperties`. The checker reads them; the structural lane never does. The checker merge only turns a source it alone found into a layer when it "proved the props type reaches it whole". Its walk stopped at every `@types/react` type, so that proof failed and "never hide on silence" listed all of them. So the `declined` guard was not the cause for this shape.

**Fix:** `composes` in `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs` now keeps walking a React type's bases. It names no extra React types, and a base the checker can't be asked for leaves those sources unproven, as before. `Button` went from 878 to 236 rows, with `VendorLonghandProperties` (224 names) and `StandardLonghandProperties` (370 names) as layers.

**Test:** `a_source_only_a_react_type_reaches_collapses_like_any_other_large_source`, built on the real `fixtures/chakra/Button.d.ts`. It passes with the fix and fails with the fix disabled. My first two test shapes passed on main too; the structural lane already handles those, so I switched to the fixture file. The test harness needed a `load_dependencies` option, added as `both_lanes_loading`.

**Remaining (about 212 rows):**
- Smaller csstype sources of 107, 76 and 26 members stay listed. They fall under the existing per-source thresholds (30 for ambient sources, 200 otherwise).
- Fixing that would mean treating a source reached only through a React type as ambient, which changes the rule in `types/ambient.rs`. It also touches the parity test against the oracle's classifier. I haven't done it.
- About 50 more rows are names React's own attribute interfaces also declare (`color`, `cursor`, `display`). The merge keeps those deliberately.

**Still to do before pushing:**
- The lint gate, workspace nextest and the checker lane.
- Output diff and memory/time against main on the fixtures.
- `/code-review medium`.

I deleted the temporary `fixtures/_tmp_styled` after use; checking that now along with the gate.

## What

A component whose props type reaches csstype through `React.CSSProperties` listed every csstype member as a row. The checker merge turns a source only the checker found into a layer of names only when the checker proved the props type reaches it whole, and the walk (`composes` in `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs`) stopped at every `@types/react` type, so csstype's interfaces under `CSSProperties` were never proven whole. "Never hide on silence" then listed them: on the Chakra fixture, `Button` had 878 rows, about 850 of them csstype's.

The walk now keeps going into a React type's bases, on the same edges that keep every member, and names no further React types. `Button` has 236 rows; `VendorLonghandProperties` (224 names) and `StandardLonghandProperties` (370) are layers.

Invariants: unknown unless proven (a React type whose bases cannot be asked for proves nothing, so what is beneath it stays listed); a source is reached whole only through the edges that keep every member (a `Pick` still selects); the `names` list is unchanged (a visit below a React type pushes none).

## Evidence

- `a_source_only_a_react_type_reaches_collapses_like_any_other_large_source` (crates/semantic/tests/relevance_model.rs), on the real `fixtures/chakra/Button.d.ts`: passes with the fix, fails with the walk into a React type's bases disabled. It finds csstype by file path, not interface names.
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0. `cargo nextest run` on the touched crates: 1515 passed. `just test-checker-lane`: exit 0.
- Output against main on all of `fixtures/` (`extract --json`, `stats` dropped): only the 8 Chakra fixture components differ; the other 44 are identical.
- Peak RSS on `fixtures/` (4 interleaved runs, load 36 to 42): main 204 to 210 MiB, this change 194 to 195 MiB; time equal within noise.
- `/code-review medium` on origin/main..HEAD: 7 items; fixed the stale doc wrapping, the obscure `known` update and the test's reliance on csstype's interface names; the rest were checked against the code and need no change (an unreached source is listed, which is the safe direction).

## Not verified

- No measurement on a real corpus (Chakra, Mantine, MUI, antd): none is cloned. The walk now asks the checker for the bases of each React type it meets, which costs a few extra requests per component; the fixtures show no time change, a large project may.
- About 212 rows of the Chakra fixture's `Button` remain from smaller csstype interfaces (107, 76, 26 and 3 members), under the per-source thresholds (30 ambient, 200 otherwise), and about 50 from names React's own attribute interfaces also declare. Treating a source reached only through a React type as ambient would collapse more; it changes `types/ambient.rs` and its parity test, and is not part of this change.
- Whether `StandardLonghandProperties` and the like stay the sources csstype splits `Properties` into in other csstype versions: the test does not depend on it.

Change D is up as PR #506 (`fix/collapse-sources-under-react-types`, head `c737aa99`), linked to trail 405, with the body published. CI and Entire Gates have not run yet. Your decisions on changes 8 and 7 are still open.

**What it does:** on the Chakra fixture, `Button` goes from 878 rows to 236. csstype's two large interfaces now collapse into layers of 224 and 370 names. `/code-review medium` gave 7 items; I fixed 3 (stale doc wrapping, an obscure `known` update, a test that relied on csstype's interface names). The other 4 I checked against the code and left alone, with reasons in the PR body.

**Checks:**
- The new test passes with the fix and fails with it disabled.
- `just lint doc-check machete typos` exits 0, and nextest on the touched crates passed (1515 tests).
- The checker lane exited 0 before the final commits, and nextest and lint were rerun after them. I did not rerun the lane on the final head.
- Output against main on all the fixtures changed only the 8 Chakra fixture components.
- Peak memory on the fixtures is a little lower (195 vs about 207 MiB). I haven't measured a real corpus, because none is cloned.

**Still open on #506:**
- About 212 rows from smaller csstype interfaces still list. Collapsing them needs a rule change in `types/ambient.rs` and its parity test.
- About 50 more rows are names React's own attribute interfaces also declare.
- Neither is part of this change, and both are stated in the PR body.

**Housekeeping:** I rebuilt main for comparison and deleted that build directory and the temp files.

needs input: three items.
1. **Change 8:** option 1, 2 or 3 for body-less components (all `.d.ts` libraries).
2. **Change 7 sizing:** whether I may clone the corpora, starting with react-spectrum. It's a multi-GB clone and install, and it's needed both for sizing change 7 and for measuring #506 on real libraries.
3. **Reviews:** #505 and #506 need your review.
What are your recommendations for the three items that require input?

My recommendation on all three, with the reason for each.

**1. Change 8, body-less components: option 1 (leave as is and say so plainly)**
- Your product rule already answers this: ambient attributes stay names unless the component uses them. A `.d.ts` component is no different from a source component whose body never reads `className`.
- Options 2 and 3 bring back the noise you rejected (about 160 rows for a MUI `Button`) or need a name list, which breaks "provenance, never names".
- The cost is real: `className` and `style` don't appear in Controls for any `.d.ts` library, which is most real design systems. Mitigate it with a note in the output that the body wasn't analysed, so the gap is stated, not silent. That fits "plain statements of what's missing" for the alpha. The note is a small follow-up I'd do after the clone.
- If you want `className` in Controls for every component, that is a separate rule change for all components, not a fix for body-less ones.

**2. Corpus clone: yes, but staged and shared**
- Check free disk first, since cloning and installing a monorepo can take several GB. I'd clone Chakra first, then react-spectrum, one at a time.
- Put them in a single shared directory (`~/.cache/caliper/corpora`, via `--corpora`), so worktrees don't each re-clone. It is a re-creatable cache, safe to delete afterwards.
- Chakra is needed to measure #506 on a real library. React-spectrum is needed to size change 7 (how many components pass `props` to a hook).
- The other three corpora, and the oracle run, can wait until after the merged batch.

**3. Reviews: merge #505 now; merge #506 after one measurement**
- #505 is docs only and low risk, so merge it whenever you've read it.
- #506 changes a hot path in the checker walk. Your own rule is to check Chakra's peak memory and time for resolver changes, and I have only fixture numbers. So after the Chakra clone I'd run main against #506 on it (about 15 minutes), then you review with real numbers. If memory or time moves, I fix that before you merge.

**Order:** your OK to clone Chakra, then the #506 measurement, then you review and merge #505 and #506. After that, react-spectrum, change 7 sizing, and the "body not analysed" note for change 8.

I'd start the Chakra clone as soon as you say go.

import os, re, sys, collections

root = sys.argv[1]
skip = ("/test/", "/stories/", "/docs/", "node_modules", "/chromatic/", "/dev/")
comp = re.compile(r"export (?:default )?(?:const|function) [A-Z]")
hand = re.compile(r"=\s*(use[A-Z]\w*)\(\s*(props|\{\s*\.\.\.props)")
hand_any = re.compile(r"\b(use[A-Z]\w*)\(\s*(props|\{\s*\.\.\.props)")
files = comps = hands = 0
hooks = collections.Counter()
examples = []
for dirpath, _, names in os.walk(root):
    if any(s in dirpath + "/" for s in skip):
        continue
    for n in names:
        if not n.endswith(".tsx"):
            continue
        text = open(os.path.join(dirpath, n), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
        files += 1
        if comp.search(text):
            comps += 1
            m = hand_any.findall(text)
            if m:
                hands += 1
                for h, _ in m:
                    hooks[h] += 1
                if len(examples) < 5:
                    examples.append(os.path.join(dirpath, n).replace(root, ""))
print("tsx files", files, "with exported component", comps, "with a useX(props) hand-off", hands)
print("top hooks", hooks.most_common(8))
print("examples", examples)

input.content:
## What

One bullet in the Storybook README's "Known limits (alpha)": the component's body decides which inherited DOM attributes get a Controls row. A body that only hands its props on whole (`useThing(props)`), or no body to read (a `.d.ts` declaration), leaves them as names in their layer; the props type's own members are always listed; `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'` lists the attributes too.

This is the plain statement for two cases I looked at and chose not to change in code (changes 8 and 7 of the road to alpha).

## Evidence

- Checked on a release build: `Handed(props: HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { own?: string })` that calls `useThing(props)` has `own` as a row and no `className` row (48 attribute names in the layer); `Reads`, which reads `props.className`, has both.
- MUI `Button` from `fixtures/mui` (a `declare const`): 26 rows with `ref` but not `className` or `style`; before #490 it listed 310.
- react-spectrum (pinned commit, `packages`): 743 of 855 component files pass `props` to a `useX(...)` hook; 593 of those calls are `useContextProps(props, ref, Context)`, which rebinds `props` and is generic over its props type, so reading a hook's parameter type would add nothing for them. The concrete-type hooks (`useRenderProps`, `useStyleProps`) consume sources the props type already declares or API sources that are listed.
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.

## Not verified

- I did not measure how many of the 743 files lose a row a user wants; the sizing counts calls, not rows.
- Whether the alpha audience wants `className` and `style` in Controls for every component is a product decision, not made here.

Beyond the three open PRs, these are the remaining items on the road to alpha, in the order I'd take them. The alpha bar is: someone installs the addon on a real design system and gets correct Controls fast on first and second start, with plain statements of what's missing.

**Needs your call first**
1. **Release recovery for 0.11.0.** The E167 `ArtifactAssetDiffers` failure is unresolved. Either delete the mismatched asset and re-run `callisto-release.yml` from main, or skip via `RELEASE_PENDING_FROM`. #497 (the release PR) is open but I haven't reviewed it, and the corpora budget gate has never run on a real release PR. Until this is settled, nobody can install an alpha.
2. **Collapse default in the first alpha.** The addon default (`collapseInheritedProps: 'dependencies'`) changes what users see: far fewer Controls rows (Chakra `Button` 1,141 → about 21), but `className` and `style` are not rows unless the body uses them. Ship it, or keep `'none'` for the first alpha? The limit is now documented in #507.
3. **Coverage floor on the weekly (#492).** The new 50% gate: does it stay?

**Product-facing, not yet measured**
4. **Storybook on a real design system.** Several measurements were never done:
   - Prefetch effect: the alpha claims fast first and second start, but only a 0.7–2.9 s checker wait was measured without it.
   - antd in Storybook: the Vite `./version` import fails.
   - Head-to-head against react-docgen-typescript.
   These are the ones that decide whether the alpha story is true, and they need your Storybook demo setup. I'd do them before inviting anyone.
5. **Weekly oracle on merged main**, once the three PRs merge. It needs mantine, shadcn and antd cloned (spectrum and chakra are done). Then refresh `docs/STATUS.md` speed numbers.
6. **The "not judged" cause** (Chakra 75.5%, Mantine 62.9%) is undiagnosed. It affects whether the headline accuracy number can be trusted.

**Known gaps in output**
7. MUI `Button` and `Select` (declared as `OverridableComponent` and `ExtendButtonBase`) aren't extracted by either binary. For a MUI user that is the first component they try, so I'd treat it as an alpha blocker for MUI. Do you want it as a slice?
8. About 212 csstype rows remain on the Chakra fixture's `Button`, plus about 50 shared-name rows. It's a rule change in `types/ambient.rs`; low priority.

**Housekeeping**
9. **Entire logs in a public repo.** All 2,585 checkpoint refs are on public origin, and one contains personal Desktop PDFs. I haven't touched it. This is the most important item that isn't product work.
10. **Local clean-up still open:** the main checkout is on a stale branch; 22 old local branches with unique commits; `wip/a518-relevant-field`.

**My recommendation:** decide 1–3 (a few minutes), then I'd do 7 (MUI extraction) and 4 (Storybook measurements) because they most affect a first user. Item 9 needs your attention separately. Tell me which to start.

Yes, and there is nothing left to do for it: the default is already `'dependencies'` on main, and changesets already describe it.

- **Already in:** `packages/storybook/src/provider.ts:47` defaults to `'dependencies'`, and the changesets `collapse-large-sources-by-default`, `list-props-by-usage` and `relevance-output` are in `.changeset/`.
- **So the decision is only whether to keep it.** Reverting to `'none'` would mean un-shipping merged work and a Chakra `Button` with 1,141 Controls rows, which is the problem the product exists to fix.
- **Why keep it:** your product rule is to list everything in the main props plus what the body uses, with ambient sources as names. That is exactly what `'dependencies'` does. The known cost is that `className` and `style` are not rows unless the body uses them, and #507 states that and the one-line escape (`collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`).
- **What to check before the alpha, not instead of it:** that someone who installs it gets a plain statement of what's missing. #507 covers the collapse limit; the three measurements (prefetch, antd, vs react-docgen-typescript) still decide whether "fast on first and second start" is true.

That leaves release recovery for 0.11.0 and the coverage floor from my first three. I'd keep the floor at 50% unless the "not judged" diagnosis shows the number misleads. Say if you'd like me to move on the release recovery next. It means reviewing #497 first, and the delete-and-re-run step is yours.

No pull-request gate enforces it: a weekly workflow records speed, memory (of the checker, the default) and recall against RDT and react-docgen, and `just bench` compares a branch with `main` locally (`docs/measurement.md`). These structural figures are by hand; the weekly's checker budgets are set after its first run.


By default the types come from TypeScript's own checker: `tsrs`, a Rust port of the TypeScript 7.1 checker, is built in, so there is nothing to install. OXC supplies what the syntax says: which components a file declares, defaults, JSDoc and the order props and union members are written in ([ADR 0026](docs/adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md)). Where the checker cannot answer, a structural resolver that reads types from the syntax alone takes over, and `--no-checker` (`checker: false`) runs it on its own.

The checker costs time. Extracting the 938 components of an app that wraps Chakra UI and MUI takes about 1.4 s and 1 GiB with the checker, 5 times as fast as `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files and harness (7.2 s, 3.8 GiB; 3.7 times on the Chakra components alone), and 0.1 s and 200 MiB with `--no-checker`; a rerun over unchanged files reuses the checker's kept answer and takes 0.25 s ([`docs/gate-measurements.md`](docs/gate-measurements.md#shared-types-a-kept-answer-and-memory-2026-11-12-perfchecker-shared-bases)). Short answer to what happened to the speed edge, plus what I'm doing about it.

**What's confirmed**
- **The 15×–39× figure was the structural resolver alone** (34–81 ms against RDT's 1.0–1.9 s, measured 2026-10-22). With the checker on, which has been the default since 2026-11-12, Caliper is 1.3–3× faster than RDT, and the README already says so. That was a deliberate trade made before today.
- **A real regression exists in the structural path as well.** I built the October commit and measured it against current main, same machine, same five corpora, same mode:

  | Corpus | October | Main now |
  |---|--:|--:|
  | Chakra | 40 ms | 140 ms |
  | Shadcn | 70 ms | 270 ms |
  | Mantine | 60 ms | 160 ms |
  | Spectrum | 130 ms | 170 ms |
  | antd | 60 ms | 50 ms (unchanged) |

  Main also spends about 4× the CPU (0.45 s against 0.11 s of user time on Chakra), and Shadcn's internal extraction doubled (73 → 138 ms).
- **I haven't pinned the cause yet.** It was not today's merges specifically: the extra work is not in the traced extraction window and the checker is off in this mode. So it is somewhere in the roughly 700 commits since 2026-10-23, and the October commit is the evidence.

**What I'm doing:** an automated bisect between the October commit and main on structural CPU time, about 10 build-and-measure steps, running in the background. It will name the commit that introduced the slowdown.

**What I will do next:** report the commit and fix it, with a test that fails when a speed budget is exceeded. The docs say the scorecard that guarded speed was removed after it failed on noisy runners, which is why nothing caught this. A CPU-time or instruction-count check is steadier than wall time under load, so I will propose that as the guard.

You asked whether we botched everything. Based on what I've measured, no: accuracy is up (shadcn 98.7% correct, about 0 wrong) and the checker default was a deliberate trade. But the structural slowdown is real, and I'm treating it as a bug to fix.

My first bisect result was wrong, so ignore the commit it named. It stopped at "load dependency declarations by default" (Oct 25, ADR 0010) because my script turned dependency loading off only on builds that also had `--no-checker`. The corrected bisect is running now in the background: the same test, but with each flag detected on its own, from that commit to main (about 9 builds).

The numbers from my earlier comparison still stand, since they were measured with explicit flags on both binaries: Chakra 40 → 140 ms, Shadcn 70 → 270 ms, Mantine 60 → 160 ms, with 4× the CPU. This bisect finds which commit caused them. I'll report the commit and the fix when it finishes.
Do we only get good speed without dependencies and the checker? Because that doesn't give us the quality results right? WTF are we doing?

Yes, the big speed numbers are for a mode that doesn't give the quality results. With dependencies off and no checker, Chakra reports 0.1% of RDT's props and about 325 unresolved names. That's the configuration where Caliper took 34–81 ms. The default (checker plus dependencies) is what gives the 99–100% own-prop recall and 88–99% correct types on the corpora, and it costs seconds. We quoted the fast mode's number next to the quality mode's results. That mismatch is the problem.

**What the quality configuration actually costs** (this morning's weekly, same corpora and machine, RDT run once cold):

| Corpus | Caliper, cold | Caliper, rerun | RDT |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| mantine | 1.14 s | 0.31 s | 1.51 s |
| shadcn | 1.91 s | 0.69 s | 4.57 s |
| antd | 1.85 s | 0.12 s | 2.88 s |
| spectrum | 2.18 s | 0.32 s | 2.81 s |
| chakra | 7.34 s (loaded machine; about 5 s unloaded) | 1.70 s | 24.04 s |

- **A cold run** is about 1.3× to 3.3× faster than RDT, with lower memory on Chakra (1.3 GiB vs 2.8 GiB) and shadcn.
- **A rerun over unchanged files** is 5× to 24× faster than RDT's cold run (the rerun reuses the checker's kept answer). This is the number that matches "fast on second start", and it is what I'd lead with.
- The Storybook claim (the first story gets structural props at once and the checker's within 150 ms) has no head-to-head measurement against RDT inside Storybook yet. That is the number the alpha story depends on.

**What I'm doing:**
- The corrected bisect is still running. A structural path that got 1.3–3.9× slower still matters, because the structural answer is what a story shows first.
- I'd rewrite the speed claims in the README and STATUS around the default configuration and name the structural-only figure as a mode, so we stop mixing them.
- I'd also measure the real experience (first story and second start) in a Storybook demo against RDT. I'll need your Storybook demo setup for that.

Say go and I'll start with the claims rewrite as a docs PR.

Yes, there are real improvements, and one of them answers your DOM question directly. Here is what the cold run costs and what I'd do, ranked by what the data supports.

**Answer to your question:** the DOM and ES libs are already baked into the binary, because the `tsrs` checker bundles TypeScript's own lib files, so they are not read from disk. React's and csstype's types are read from the project's `node_modules`, since their shape depends on the project's version. The fixed cost of all of that is small: a two-component project takes 30 ms structural against 40 ms with the checker. So caching lib or React types would not move cold start, and I'm not proposing it.

**Where a cold default run goes** (shadcn, 2.06 s wall, 6.6 CPU-seconds):
- **The checker phase is CPU-heavy, not serial:** CPU is 1.6–3.2× wall across the corpora.
- **32,251 requests for 1,802 components,** about 18 per component.
- **Where the busy CPU goes:** `tsrs` checking itself is only 14.5%, the JSON codec for checker requests is 21.4%, allocation and copying 24.8%, file and VFS reads 10.1%, and parsing, binding and symbols 6.9%. Cause: `tsrs_api` is a Rust port of TypeScript's JSON API server, so every request and answer is JSON text even in-process.

**Ranked improvements**
1. **Stop building HTML attributes that relevance folds away.** This is the structural regression I found (Chakra 40 → 170 ms, CPU 80 → 380 ms). It saves about 130 ms of the structural answer (6% of a cold default run), and the structural answer is what a story shows first. Risk is moderate: it touches the resolver and how relevance promotes members, so I'd verify identical output on all five corpora plus the snapshot tests before merging.
2. **Cut the request count.** Batch the checker walk's separate calls (`base_types`, `alias_type_arguments`, `parts`) and memoize results by type id across components. My #506 adds a few of those requests per component, so a memo also pays that back. The gain is unmeasured until I count requests by method.
3. **Resolver memo.** About 20,000 resolver calls for 1,385 files, resolving the same specifiers repeatedly. Dependency loading adds roughly 180 ms over structural alone, but I can't say how much a memo recovers.
4. **Call the checker directly instead of through JSON.** This could remove the 21% codec cost and a large part of the allocation cost. It is a large rewrite of the converter, so I would not start it without your decision.

**Unexplained:** about 250 ms before the first component answers, which I couldn't attribute.

content.text:
No, the goal wasn't lost, and the full-attributes default is a recorded decision. I have no record of a decision to walk it back, so tell me if one was made somewhere I can't see.

**What's recorded**
- **The goal** was that a reader shouldn't see every DOM attribute as a Controls row. That is done: with the collapse default and relevance, a Chakra `Button` shows about 21 rows, and the attributes are names in a layer. We did walk back what the reader sees.
- **ADR 0028** says the `htmlAttributes` setting controls which DOM attributes are known, as rows or layer names, not how many rows a reader sees. It also says `full` stays the default, because a passed attribute can be a typed row only if it is known. If a body reads `props.onFocus` or `aria-label`, that attribute needs a type to become a row. `curated` knows only a compact subset, so such a read outside the list would get no typed row.
- My memory notes contain nothing about this setting either way.

**What I found in the measurement**
- `full` is cheap to reason about and expensive to run: it builds the type for about 285 attributes per component, and then relevance throws nearly all of them into the layer. Structural `full` on Chakra is 170 ms against `curated` at 90 ms and `none` at 40 ms.
- So the issue is not "we kept something we agreed to drop". It's that the implementation does the work before the decision, not after.

**Options, and my recommendation**
1. **Lazy build (recommended).** Keep `full` semantics: any attribute a body uses can be a typed row. Build the attribute's type only for the ones relevance keeps. The output stays identical, and I'd prove that on all five corpora. It recovers most of the 130 ms.
2. **Change the default to `curated`.** It is cheaper and simpler, but it changes the product: a read attribute outside the curated list gets no row, and output on existing users' projects shifts. This contradicts the ADR, so it should be a deliberate decision, with an ADR amendment.
3. **`none`.** Fastest, but no DOM attribute can ever be a row, even one the component uses. I don't think that's what you want.

If what you meant was option 2 or 3, say so and I'll write the ADR amendment before touching code. Otherwise I'll treat option 1 as the plan.
